item.description:

Stop overcomplicating tf out of facebook ads.. Here’s a structure that actually works (and scales fast): - 1 CBO Campaign w/ $100 Daily Budget - 3 Ad Sets — Broad. No targeting. - 3 Creatives Per Adset The creatives in each adset should focus on a different angle. Skin Lotion Example: • Ad Set 1 – “Eye Bags” • Ad Set 2 – “Saggy Skin” • Ad Set 3 – “Old & Aging” Each Creative Includes The Same: • 3 Primary Texts • 2 Headlines • 1 Description Now let the algorithm go to work. Its only job? Find your winner. Once an adset (angle) starts to perform duplicate it & load it with fresh creatives around that same angle Meta will automatically shift spend to the best performers. After a bit of consistency scale your CBO: $100 → $250 → $500 → $1,000+ Keep feeding your CBO with better inputs: New creatives with new angles, better hooks, etc. Simple structure. Just a game of creative testing.

item.title:
One of our low-ticket funnels cracked $1M in the last 90 days.
And that’s with a 2.2X ROAS on JU...
item.description:
@undefined

One of our low-ticket funnels cracked $1M in the last 90 days. And that’s with a 2.2X ROAS on JUST the front-end. One of the biggest needle-movers for scaling any funnel on Facebook ads is the sheer volume of creative testing. While most marketers barely launch 5-10 creatives per week, we currently have 490 ad creatives running for this offer. Yes, 490 creatives, and we'll probably be at 1,000+ in the next two months. The easiest way to bulk-test creatives is to knock out 100+ hooks at a time and then pair them with ~10 different body copy variations. The hook does 80% of the selling. For image ads, you want to test dozens upon dozens of different concepts with ~5-10 different hook variations. For video ads, we typically fly out to our partners and record ~100-150 hooks in one-take (only takes around 15-20 minutes) and then edit them into different body copy variations. Here’s an example of different angles we test: Problem/pain point angles Contrarian/myth-busting angles Solution/method reveal angles Transformation/outcome angles Authority/social proof angles Curiosity/intrigue angles Fear of missing out angles Contrast/before-after angles Emotional/identity angles Question/challenge angles Mistake/warning angles Outcome-focused / demonstrable hooks Pattern interrupt/shock value You can throw those into AI / Claude, have it knock out 25 variations of each, and get countless hook variations for testing. Easier than you think and absolutely critical for scaling offers to multi 6-figures /month 👊

item.description:
@undefined

There’s one mistake I see most ecom brands make with Facebook ads that keeps them stuck at $1K/day. They think more creative testing = better results. But here’s the truth after scaling multiple brands to $1M/month: Most ad accounts aren’t broken because of bad creatives… They’re broken because the creative strategy is wrong. You’re iterating on burned-out winners for months straight. Fix that and scaling becomes easy. Brand was stuck at $1K/day for 4 months. They had a winning ad—so they kept iterating on it. New text. New edits. New thumbnails. All based on the same core message. But nothing scaled… Until we did one thing: We went back to the market. We stopped trying to out-edit the winner and started doing actual market research. What desires weren’t we speaking to? What objections were still unaddressed? We found a new desire people deeply wanted but no one was talking about it. So we filmed new creatives around that. Boom: $1K/day → $10K/day in 30 days. Here’s what that taught me: 📌 If performance is stuck, stop iterating and go find a new big swing. ✅ A new desire ✅ A new symptom ✅ A new positioning that makes the product feel NEW again Then test that with fresh creatives. That’s how you unlock scale. Another example: lead gen client spending $10K/day. ROAS was slipping. We tested hundreds of aware/problem-aware ads. Then I looked at ad frequency: 1.6, 1.7, 1.8... Time to reach a colder audience. We pivoted to unaware creatives. Big fear hook. Educated into the problem. Then pitched the solution. CPA dropped $10 overnight. Scaling isn’t just about media buying. It’s about: → Knowing when to pivot→ And making bold creative decisions based on desire, not just data That’s how we scale brands to $1M/month. item.title:
“My ads aren’t getting more than $5-10 of spend in the CBO…”
If you’re running Facebook ads and ...
item.description:
@undefined

“My ads aren’t getting more than $5-10 of spend in the CBO…” If you’re running Facebook ads and you’ve said this to yourself recently—read every word of this. Because I’ve looked at hundreds of accounts and it’s almost never the media buying that’s the problem. It’s the creative. Let’s break it down. When a new ad isn’t getting spend inside your CBO, it’s almost always because the creative isn’t engaging. Not engaging = no dopamine. No dopamine = no attention. Facebook wants to give your best ad more money. But you have to earn it. Here’s what’s really happening: Most of the time, the new ads you’re testing aren’t just “not good enough”… they’re nowhere close to your current winner. So of course Facebook keeps funneling spend into the winner—it’s the only one firing dopamine, stopping thumbs, and converting attention into action. And the worst part? Most brands keep testing creatives that never even had a shot in the first place. Here’s what I look at when an ad isn’t getting spend: 1. Does it SHOW what people want? Not just say it—visually show the transformation, the desire, the outcome. That’s what fires dopamine. You’ve got milliseconds to stop the scroll. Make it count. 2. Are you calling it out CLEARLY? If your hook isn’t instantly understood by your least-interested prospect, it won’t work. Great hooks create instant clarity and curiosity. 3. Are you testing against your best performer—or just testing to test? The goal of testing is to beat the control, not throw random stuff at the wall. If your winner is elite, your test creative needs to be a real contender—not filler. 4. Are you speaking too narrowly? If the creative is too specific—like someone who’s visited your site 3 times and is waiting for a 15% discount—you’re capping TAM. That doesn’t scale. Facebook rewards reach. 5. Are you creating new neural pathways? This is the real sauce: dopamine is created by novelty. If your market has seen the same creative style 500 times—even if it’s not from you—it won’t fire dopamine. No dopamine = no spend. New experiences create new brain activity. That’s why reinventing the wheel in your ad—positioning it to feel fresh, unexpected, different—is what lets it scale. 6. Are your creatives in a red ocean or a blue one? If your ad looks like every other brand in your niche, why would Facebook favor you? Blue ocean positioning visually separates you. It triggers that primal “wait, what’s this?” response. That’s what gets the spend. 7. Are your personas built for scale? Not every persona has the same TAM. Ads targeting mass-market desires (not hyper-specific segments) will almost always get more spend. Persona matters—but scale matters more. TL;DR When your ads aren’t getting spend, stop blaming the algorithm. Start asking: •Are we visually and emotionally showing something people actually want? •Are we triggering dopamine with novelty and clarity? •Are we creating new neural pathways—or just recycling what everyone else is doing? The CBO isn’t broken. Your creative strategy is. Fix that—and the spend will follow.

...
item.description:
@undefined

Most brands sleep on their front-end OFFER… until they see what happens when they get it right. Having a performance-focused funnel is not just about optimizing conversion rate The key metric is Revenue per visitor Which is CVR x AOV One good offer can boost your paid ads profitability and unlock new levels of scale ➜ Here are the top 6 e-commerce offers working right now 👇 Before diving into the different types of offers, keep these key principles in mind: A) The offer should match the funnel stage of the traffic (an offer for TOF acquisition will differ from one for existing buyers) B) The offer should be optimized for increasing perceived value (i.e. make it a “no-brainer “ whatever the price they pay) C) How you PRESENT the offer is as important as the offer itself (design, copywriting, etc) D ) It's all about testing. Never assume what will/will not work. Make an intentional hypothesis > test and validate Now let’s dive into the top 6 types of offers you should test ➜ 1 - BOGO: BUY 1 GET 1 FREE ( OR BUY X GET Y FREE) This one is powerful especially if it makes sense to buy multiple units of your products (Supplements, consumables, beauty products, etc) By the way, mathematically BUY 1 GET 1 FREE is similar as BUY 1 and get 50% OFF So if you can't afford to offer another unit for free, If you play with the numbers, you can come up with other interesting offers like BUY 2 GET 1 FREE, BUY 4 GET 2 FREE, etc. It’s about how you present it more about the actual discount. ➜ 2 - THE STARTER KIT (OR FREE GIFTS) If you have accessories or complementary products that help achieve the SAME OUTCOME that the primary product offers; Testing a starter kit is a no-brainer. You can also add the accessories as free gifts. Which will increase the perceived value of the offer AND the perceived likelihood of achieving the promised outcome. ➜ 3 - VALUE AMOUNT/DISCOUNT OFF This is a common one. Overused with dropshipping stores pushing discounts from 50 to 90% OFF.. The only way to make it attractive is to give a BELIEVABLE justification behind the offer. For example: Black Friday Sale, Launch Offer, etc.. Without this, it may come across as fake scarcity because your traffic is not dumb. I would rarely go with this one unless it's your only option. ➜ 4 - QUANTITY BUNDLE This one is a classic but very powerful Never sell one when you can offer more for a discount. A higher AOV will set you apart in the paid ads game The brand who can spend the most to acquire customers is the brand who wins Make sure you create PRICE ANCHORING to incentivize the traffic to go for the higher value bundle The idea is to get them to feel “stupid” to go with the cheapest option ➜ 5 - QUANTITY BUNDLE (ALTERNATIVE) Instead of using price anchoring to position higher-value bundles as no brainers, you can add free gifts for customers who buy more Sometimes it requires custom coding but this gamification can work pretty well for consumable products The more the gifts make sense with the product they're buying, the better. ➜ 6 - (ADVANCED) TRY BEFORE YOU BUY This one is more advanced, you need to have a solid understanding of your unit economics, finances and cash flow. Customers pay only for shipping upfront, (which skyrockets your conversion rate) You’d bill them the full offer price (e.g. $49.95) automatically after a set period (e.g. 21 days) if they keep the product (i.e. they don’t return it). You can also push it a step further & set it as a subscription to capitalize on LTV too. - That's a wrap I hope you found this insightful - If you run a DTC brand and want to scale your paid ads through funnels/landing pages 👉https://t.co/YSTiRfjU7H - 1.
